generated_note: Hand-maintained. Nothing publishes ATP Challenger or ITF draws in a machine-readable feed; the calendar was parsed once from the 2026 ATP Challenger Tour and 2026 WTA 125 calendars and cross-checked against api.wtatennis.com for tour level.

venue_scale.note: Kalshi figures are contracts at $1 notional summed across both per-player books. Polymarket is dollar trade value on the single moneyline market. Cross-venue absolute levels are NOT comparable; rankings within a venue are.

growth_factor.note: 2025 -> current platform. The anchor is unreliable: the US Open pair gives 2.8x on raw per-match but 8.1x depth-matched, because its listing went from 170 to 532 matches. An earlier 2.1-3.4x estimate was withdrawn - it rested on a Guangzhou pair that compared the WTA 250 against the men's Challenger of the same city.

before_you_list: Confirm the listing layer can carry ATP Challenger and ITF events. Many sports integrations key off per-tour identifiers that only cover ATP and WTA main tour, and every slot-1 pick here is a Challenger.
Confirm a settlement feed exists for Challenger and ITF results. Tour-level result feeds are well covered; sub-tour is thinner and resolution risk is the main operational cost of this plan.

evidence_classes.C: 2025 only, platform 3-8x smaller - rank order more reliable than level
evidence_classes.D: Listed and dead - the strongest negative signal

confidence.measured: this event has its own settled history
confidence.range: no history for this event; range from tier and region
confidence.none: never listed anywhere - the number is a regional prior, not a measurement

sub_tour_per_match.note: Kalshi notional per match, which is the fair way to compare tiers - total volume just tracks how many tournaments there are.
sub_tour_per_match.verdict: A median Challenger is 3.3x a median ITF event per match and 5.4x per slot-week. That is why slot 1 is a Challenger every week - not because ITF is a weak product.

itf.why_not_on_the_grid: No source publishes ITF draws with dates. The WTA API carries ITF but none of its rows reach this window, and there is no equivalent men's feed. ITF is absent from the calendar for that reason ALONE - it is not a recommendation against listing it.
itf.region_note: The regional signal is the OPPOSITE of the Challenger one. Challengers pay in North America (~2.4x); ITF pays in Asia-Pacific, and Europe - which is 193 of 216 ITF events - is the weakest at $119,701 per match. The $257,975 ITF median is dragged down by that European tail.
itf.selection_rule: If you list ITF, take an Asia-Pacific M15/M25 or W35 (Bali, Tianjin, Brisbane, Astana, Taipei, Maanshan, Kyoto, Sao Paulo). Tournament choice is worth 1.83x in ITF. Avoid European W15s at $119,701 a match - they are 193 of 216 ITF events and the reason the category median looks poor.
itf.when_it_wins: ITF is the overflow tier. With only 1-2 slots a Challenger wins every week, including December when the Challenger slate drops to Challenger 50s (still ~$20M a week). ITF becomes the right answer if the slot count ever rises above two, or as the filler after the Challenger season ends on 13 December - ITF runs straight through the holidays.

per_match_distribution.note: Kalshi, both sides summed, 11,571 ITF matches vs 2,463 Challenger matches over ten weeks. The median understates ITF badly - it is a fat-tailed distribution and the mean is 2.8x the median (Challenger 1.8x).
per_match_distribution.headline: ITF produces MORE $1M+ matches in absolute terms than the whole Challenger tour (995 vs 803), because there are 4.7x as many of them. Its single biggest match ($11.1M, a W35 Sao Paulo) beats the biggest Challenger match ($9.9M). 17.3% of ITF matches clear the Challenger median, and those carry 66% of all ITF volume.

selectability.question: The tail is real - but can you pick it in advance?
selectability.verdict: Partly. Choosing a good ITF tournament lifts the median match 1.83x (Challenger only 1.44x), so tournament selection matters MORE in ITF. But a well-chosen ITF event still medians $220,754 a match against $560,211 for a Challenger match picked at random - a 2.5x gap that tournament selection does not close. And 45% of an ITF tournament's volume sits in five matches you cannot identify before the draw.

worked_example.match: Ohashi vs Yodpetch, W35 Kyoto, Round of 32, 16 Sep 2026
worked_example.note: A first-round match at a $35,000 event did $2.85M. That is ITF's p99, not a freak: 297 ITF matches cleared $2M in ten weeks, about 30 a week. It is also Asia-Pacific, consistent with the regional split.
